summary_ja: 中核的市場参加者を相手とする国債等・現金によるレポ取引で、同一通貨・翌日終了又は日次値洗い等の要件を全て満たすものはボラティリティ調整率の適用を要しないとし、中核的市場参加者を列挙する。
summary_en: Zero haircut for repos with core market participants in cash or 0%-RW sovereign paper, same currency, overnight or daily-margined, with fast liquidation and standard documentation; lists the core market participants.
paragraphs: For repo-style transactions that satisfy all of the following requirements, an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach is not required to apply haircuts in the formula of Article 67 or Article 80. (i) That the repo-style transaction is a transaction with a core market participant as counterparty. (ii) That both the exposure and the eligible financial collateral are cash, deposits, or bonds issued by central governments, etc. and local governments in Japan to which a 0% risk weight applies under the standardized approach. (iii) That the exposure and the eligible financial collateral are denominated in the same currency. (iv) That the repo-style transaction terminates on the business day following the date on which it is executed, or that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach marks both the exposure and the eligible financial collateral to market every business day and they are subject to margin calls. (v) That, where the counterparty fails to meet a margin call and the collateral is disposed of, the number of days from the date of the marking to market for that margin call until the collateral can be disposed of is four business days or less. (vi) That the reliability of the external system used to process the settlement of the transaction is ensured. (vii) That the transaction satisfies the contractual form generally used for transactions of the same type among core market participants. (viii) That it is specified in writing that the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach can terminate the transaction immediately if the counterparty fails to perform its obligation to deliver cash or securities, to provide additional collateral or another obligation. (ix) That, where an event allowing the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach to terminate the transaction (including the counterparty's failure to perform an obligation to deliver cash or securities, to provide additional collateral or another obligation, and the occurrence of insolvency, a decision to commence bankruptcy proceedings, a decision to commence rehabilitation proceedings, a decision to commence reorganization proceedings, an order to commence special liquidation or similar events) occurs for the counterparty, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach has the right to dispose of the collateral immediately.

"Core market participants" in the preceding paragraph means the following. (i) Central governments, etc., local governments in Japan, the Japan Finance Organization for Municipalities, Japanese government-affiliated agencies and public sector entities other than foreign central governments. (ii) Financial institutions (excluding persons listed in Article 1, item (vii)(b) and (f)), foreign banks, bank holding companies, foreign companies equivalent to bank holding companies, Type I financial instruments business operators whose risk weight is provided in Article 31, foreign companies equivalent to Ultimate Designated Parent Companies, management companies and foreign securities firms, securities finance companies, money market brokers designated by the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency under Article 1-2, item (iii) of the Order for Enforcement of the Money Lending Business Act (Cabinet Order No. 181 of 1983), and multilateral development banks not falling under the preceding item. (iii) Of the companies listed in Article 16-2, paragraph (1), items (v), (v-2) and (ix) of the Banking Act, those to which a 20% risk weight applies under the standardized approach. (iv) Investment trusts, etc. subject to capital regulation or to regulation restricting the leveraging of investment effects through borrowing or the use of derivative transactions. (v) Surviving employees' pension funds (meaning surviving employees' pension funds provided in Article 3, item (xi) of the Supplementary Provisions of the Act Partially Amending the Employees' Pension Insurance Act, etc. to Ensure the Soundness and Reliability of the Public Pension System (Act No. 63 of 2013)) and the Pension Fund Association. (vi) Financial instruments clearing organizations.
